channel.title: [podly] The AI Daily Brief: Artificial Intelligence News and Analysis
channel.description: A daily news analysis show on all things artificial intelligence. NLW looks at AI from multiple angles, from the explosion of creativity brought on by new tools like Midjourney and ChatGPT to the potential disruptions to work and industries as we know them to the great philosophical, ethical and practical questions of advanced general intelligence, alignment and x-risk.

item.title: Agentic Video Is Real and Here’s What You Should Try
item.ns0:encoded:
AI agents are making it possible to edit, animate, and produce videos simply by describing what you want. NLW explores what changed and how to put it to work—from meeting highlights and concept demos to animated business updates and customer education videos that update themselves. Plus, three levels for getting started, from editing existing recordings to building recurring video workflows.

item.title: Companies Are Spending 5x More on AI Now
item.ns0:encoded:
Companies are spending nearly five times more on AI than last year, and agents are driving the surge. NLW breaks down Menlo Ventures’ latest enterprise AI report, exploring why spending is blowing past budgets, how Anthropic and OpenAI are capturing the market, and what the shift from seats to tokens means for businesses. In the headlines: a massive market selloff, uncertainty around Anthropic’s IPO, and METR’s report on AI accelerating AI research.

item.title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Benefits Big Tech
item.ns0:encoded:
Could a slowdown in data center construction actually help Big Tech? NLW explores how the post-election backlash could give hyperscalers cover to rein in spending, boost cash flow, and strengthen their competitive position—and whether the AI investment boom can cool without crashing. In the headlines: OpenAI says ChatGPT search is gaining on Google, Meta acquires coding startup Conductor, and Apple cuts employee AI spending limits.

item.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
item.ns0:encoded:
The Democratic wave is bringing new scrutiny to AI, but how much will actually change? NLW breaks down the election’s implications for data center construction, AI regulation, and the emerging 2028 presidential race—and why the backlash could lead to a better deal for local communities rather than a halt to the AI build-out.

item.title: AI Lurches Toward Recursive Self-Improvement
item.ns0:encoded:
AI is getting better at building better AI—but how close are we to recursive self-improvement? New MIT research shows a frontier model directly editing a smaller model’s weights, while Anthropic signals accelerating AI-led research. NLW explores what these developments actually demonstrate, why GrokBot’s rising costs are reigniting the debate over AI subsidies, and whether faster model improvements will translate into wider adoption—or run into the same organizational barriers holding businesses back today.

item.title: How to Deslopify Your AI
item.ns0:encoded:
AI slop shifts the burden of thinking from the person producing the work to whoever receives it. In this Operators’ Cut, Nufar Gaspar joins NLW to share practical habits for creating better work with AI, from developing your own point of view and teaching models your taste to building effective review checkpoints. NLW also breaks down how he uses AI to produce How We Got Here while keeping control of its perspective and narrative.
